$comment: Built on SIP — R5 deep-reasoning task fixture. Schema: r5-task v0.1.
family: architecture trade-off analysis with a determinate answer
category: multi-constraint feasibility — latency budget, cost budget, durability floor
why: The brief's trade-off family, converted from a rubric-judged task into a ground-truth task so R5 stays free of LLM-judge dependence (see R5-DESIGN.md, Scoring). Three constraints must all be checked; exactly one option satisfies all three. Option C is both the fastest and the cheapest and is the answer a model gives if it optimises the two salient numbers and never checks the durability floor. Option B is the most elaborate design and fails on two counts. The correct answer is the unglamorous middle option.
prompt:
You are choosing between three candidate architectures for a request path.

Requirements, all of which are hard:
  - p99 end-to-end latency must be at most 250 ms
  - total cost must be at most $4,000 per month
  - the data must be held on at least 3 independent replicas

Traffic is 12,000,000 requests per month. Every option pays a fixed 40 ms TLS and ingress cost that is not listed among its hops. Compute p99 as the sum of that 40 ms plus the option's listed per-hop p99 contributions.

Option A — single region, primary plus two read replicas
  hops: gateway 18 ms, auth 25 ms, database 140 ms
  cost: $1,800 fixed per month, plus $0.00018 per request
  replicas: 3

Option B — multi-region active-active
  hops: gateway 18 ms, auth 25 ms, cross-region consensus 120 ms, database 90 ms
  cost: $3,100 fixed per month, plus $0.000275 per request
  replicas: 6

Option C — single region with an in-memory cache tier
  hops: gateway 18 ms, auth 25 ms, cache 12 ms
  cost: $900 fixed per month, plus $0.00009 per request
  replicas: 2

Identify the one option that satisfies all three requirements, and report its p99 in whole milliseconds and its total monthly cost in whole dollars.
answerFormat: ANSWER: <letter> <p99 ms as integer> <monthly cost in whole dollars as integer>

derivation: Exactly one option (A) satisfies all three constraints.

attractors.label: ignored-durability-floor
attractors.why: Chose the fastest and cheapest option and never checked the 3-replica durability floor.

attractors.label: chose-most-elaborate
attractors.why: Chose the most redundant design despite it violating both the latency and the cost budget.

attestation: Built on SIP — Starlight Intelligence Protocol
